output.summary: KEP-1623 standardized a common Condition type (Type, Status, ObservedGeneration, LastTransitionTime, Reason, Message) in k8s.io/apimachinery meta/v1 for use in .status.conditions across new APIs, plus shared helper methods. Status: implemented, stable.
output.rationale: Condition schemas varied widely across Kubernetes APIs, so consumers could not rely on a common shape and could not share Get/Set/Is logic. The KEP proposes a fixed golang type for new APIs to be embedded literally, and the discussion notes it standardizes existing practice rather than inventing a new one. Reviewers accepted compatibility trade-offs (e.g., metav1.Time rather than MicroTime, non-pointer required-but-empty fields) to ease consumer adoption.

alternatives.option: Recommend a schema without providing a shared type
alternatives.why_not: The KEP says this 'doesn't seem very nice to consumers.'
deads2k argued that consumers are used to normal time and the gain did not warrant the pain; the KEP keeps metav1.Time.

alternatives.option: Make Condition fields optional pointers (e.g., *bool for status, *string for message)
alternatives.why_not: deads2k wanted to avoid pointers in a commonly used struct; the field set was kept non-pointer with the zero value treated as valid for some fields.
deads2k was -1 because identity can be obtained via the fieldManager and duplicating it was undesired.

evidence.quote: Conditions are central enough to the API to make a common golang type with a fixed schema. The schema can be a strong recommendation to all API authors.
This is not strictly compatible with any of our existing conditions because of either proto ordinals, required vs optional, or omitEmpty or not.
This enhancement is just about having a recommended data structure to avoid having subtly different ones everywhere forever.
The rule is, the zero value is sufficiently invalid that it doesn't create any ambiguity. Omitted-on-the-wire needs to mean "I have no opinion".
It gives an option for acknowledging awareness of a condition without the ability to inspect the current value.
